title: Single-Threaded CPU Order
statement:
Return the order in which a single worker processes indexed tasks.

Contract
- `tasks` is non-null. Each row is exactly `[enqueueTime, processingTime]` with non-negative times, and the row index is the task id.
- Whenever the worker is free, it may run any task whose enqueue time is at or before the current time.
- Choose the available task with the smallest processing time; break ties by the smallest original index. If none is available, jump time to the next enqueue time.
- Return every task index in the order processing starts. Do not mutate `tasks`.

Examples
- `processingOrder(new int[][]{{1,2},{2,4},{3,2},{4,1}})` returns `[0, 2, 3, 1]`.
- Tasks `[[7,10],[7,12],[7,5],[7,4],[7,2]]` return `[4, 3, 2, 0, 1]`.
- One task returns `[0]`.
hints: Sort task ids by enqueue time so tasks become visible in chronological order.
Keep available tasks in a priority queue ordered by processing time, then by original index.
When the queue is empty, advance the clock to the next enqueue time. Intended complexity: O(n log n) time and O(n) space.
inputSyntax: Input: task pairs [enqueue, processing] in order, for example: [[1, 2], [2, 4], [3, 2], [4, 1]]
